Definition: from G5571 and G80; a spurious brother, i.e. pretended associate:--false brethren.
BiblicalUsage: Pseudadelphos means a false brother, a pretended associate. Paul lists his perils, in perils among false brethren, and says false brethren were brought in unawares to spy out the liberty the Galatians had in Christ Jesus, that they might bring them into bondage.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the false brother is more dangerous than the open enemy, because he comes inside the walls and spies out the liberty he wants to take away.
